text: If your cat ever knocks on your bedroom door... do not open it.
Do not get up. Do not turn on the light. Do not say its name.
It is three twelve in the morning. It will knock three times. It always knocks three times.
There are seven rules. You already follow two of them. You just don't know why.
Rule one. Do not open the door.
Listen to where the knock comes from. Not the bottom of the door. The middle.
A cat that wants in will scratch. It will push. It will cry.
It will not knock. Cats do not knock.
This one knocks at the height of your hand.
Rule two. Do not say its name.
You will want to. Is that you? Do not.
In twenty nineteen, researchers in Japan showed that cats know their own names. They hear it. They understand it.
Your cat has heard you say its name every day for years.
So has whatever is outside your door.
Rule three. Do not look under the door.
There is a light in the hallway. You did not leave it on.
In the gap under the door, you will see the shadow of feet. Count them.
A cat has four.
Stop counting.
Rule four. When it meows, do not answer.
Here is something most people never notice. Grown cats almost never meow at each other.
The meow is not cat language. It is a sound cats made for us.
Something outside your door has been listening to that sound for a long time.
It is close. It is not quite right yet. It sounds a little like your cat. It sounds a little like you.
Rule five. Before you do anything else, look at the foot of your bed.
Your cat is there. It has been there all night.
Then what is knocking?
One moment.
We may continue.
Rule six. From now on, do not watch the door. Watch your cat.
Cats hear sounds far higher than you can. Footsteps you will never hear. Breathing you will never hear.
In twenty thirteen, a study found that cats know their owner's voice. When you call, they hear you. Most of them do not come. They only turn their ears.
Tonight, your cat is not ignoring you. It is listening to something else.
If its ears point at the door, do not move. If its tail gets big, do not breathe loudly.
If it puts its head down and closes its eyes... it is gone.
Your cat will tell you when. It always has. You thought it was just sleeping.
Rule seven.
We will come back to rule seven.
In the morning, your cat will sit by the bedroom door and wait for you to open it. Open it. That one is safe.
Look at the door before you go. Near the middle. At the height of your hand.
Three marks. Like paw prints. Too far apart to be paws.
Your cat did not sleep last night. It sat at the foot of your bed and watched the door until the light went out.
It has done this before. You have never once thanked it.
Rule eight is for the night your cat is not on the bed.
Thank you for listening. Lock your door.
